subject: Log scale minor grid line default behavior

messages.author: f99b567edf86f024
messages.subject: Log scale minor grid line default behavior
parts:
Hello ggplot2,

These days people are making a lot of log scale plots. 
ggplot by default creates a minor grid line that is visually midway between the major grid lines.  I find this behavior to be either misleading or confusing (it's hard to compute in your head what's midway in log space between 100 and 1000).  The answer is 316 (see Fig 1).  To address this I've created a new log scale that places minor grid lines either at each integer space (Fig 2) or midway in a linear scale (Fig 3).   I find these new scales much more intuitive and less likely to mislead.  
The reason why I'm sending this message is to see if others agree that this would be useful.  If so I'll invest the effort into preparing a pull request and making the code more robust.  Otherwise it'll live in my private util script.

Code to recreate figures are below.

Thanks,

Amit

ggplot(data.frame(x=c(100,316,500,1000,10000),y=c(1,2,3,4,5)),aes(x=x,y=y)) + geom_point() + geom_text(aes(label = x),position = position_nudge(y =+0.15))+ scale_x_log10(limits=c(100,10000))

ggplot(data.frame(x=c(100,316,500,1000,10000),y=c(1,2,3,4,5)),aes(x=x,y=y)) + geom_point() + geom_text(aes(label = x),position = position_nudge(y =+0.15))+ scale_x_log_alt(limits=c(100,10000))

ggplot(data.frame(x=c(100,316,500,1000,10000),y=c(1,2,3,4,5)),aes(x=x,y=y)) + geom_point() + geom_text(aes(label = x),position = position_nudge(y =+0.15))+ scale_x_log_alt(midonly=FALSE,limits=c(100,10000))

log_breaks = function(maj, base=10,midonly=TRUE) {
  function(x) {
    minx         = floor(min(logb(x,base), na.rm=T)) - 1
    maxx         = ceiling(max(logb(x,base), na.rm=T)) + 1
    n_major      = maxx - minx + 1
    major_breaks = seq(minx, maxx, by=1)
    if (maj) {
      breaks = major_breaks
    }
​
    else {
      if (midonly) {steps = logb(base/2.0,base)}
      else{steps=logb(1:(base-1),base)}
      breaks = rep(steps, times=n_major) +
               rep(major_breaks, each=base-1)
    }
    base^breaks
  }
}
scale_x_log_alt = function(..., base=10,midonly=TRUE) {
  scale_x_continuous(...,
                     trans=log_trans(base),
                     breaks=log_breaks(TRUE, base,mid),
                     minor_breaks=log_breaks(FALSE, base,midonly))
}
scale_y_log_alt = function(..., base=10,midonly=TRUE) {
  scale_y_continuous(...,
                     trans=log_trans(base),
                     breaks=log_breaks(TRUE, base,midonly),
                     minor_breaks=log_breaks(FALSE, base,midonly))
}
